headline: Australia's coach admits Bangladesh wins first Test in Australia
summary: Australia's head coach Andrew McDonald admits the team played poorly and failed to maintain their standards after a historic victory for Bangladesh.
details: Bangladesh has achieved a historic milestone by winning their first-ever Test match in Australia, defeating the hosts in Darwin.
The victory was dominant throughout the match, with Australia being bowled out for 198 in their first innings, trailing Bangladesh by 226 runs.
In the second innings, Australia managed to set a target of only 57 runs, which Bangladesh chased down while losing only one wicket.
Australia's head coach Andrew McDonald expressed deep disappointment, stating that scoring less than 500 runs across two innings on such a pitch was unacceptable.
The defeat has sparked calls for change within the Australian team, with former cricketer Ricky Ponting suggesting changes to the opening and number three positions.
Other former cricketers have urged the national team to integrate more young players, noting that only Cameron Green was under 30 years old in the squad.
Coach McDonald acknowledged the team's age balance and the team's ongoing discussions about the future direction of the team.
Despite the calls for changes, McDonald believes that the current players still have a lot of cricket left in them and that it is natural for critics to demand changes after a loss.
caption:
A historic first for Bangladesh! 🇧🇩
Australia's coach admits they played poorly after a dominant win by the Tigers.

Bangladesh has achieved a historic milestone by winning their first-ever Test match in Australia, defeating the hosts in Darwin.

The victory was dominant throughout the match, with Australia being bowled out for 198 in their first innings, trailing Bangladesh by 226 runs.

In the second innings, Australia managed to set a target of only 57 runs, which Bangladesh chased down while losing only one wicket.

Australia's head coach Andrew McDonald expressed deep disappointment, stating that scoring less than 500 runs across two innings on such a pitch was unacceptable.

The defeat has sparked calls for change within the Australian team, with former cricketer Ricky Ponting suggesting changes to the opening and number three positions.

Other former cricketers have urged the national team to integrate more young players, noting that only Cameron Green was under 30 years old in the squad.

Coach McDonald acknowledged the team's age balance and the team's ongoing discussions about the future direction of the team.

Despite the calls for changes, McDonald believes that the current players still have a lot of cricket left in them and that it is natural for critics to demand changes after a loss.

headline_marked: Cabinet approves draft to [[abolish RAB and form SRB]]
headline: Cabinet approves draft to abolish RAB and form SRB
summary: The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) will be replaced by the Special Response Battalion (SRB), a specialized unit under the police force.
details: The cabinet has granted final approval to the draft of the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026', following vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.
Under this new law, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) will be abolished and replaced by the Special Response Battalion (SRB), which will operate as a specialized unit under the police force.
The act includes provisions for a multi-party grievance redressal committee to resolve complaints from citizens and internal conflicts among unit members.
All manpower, orders, powers, authority, benefits, funds, properties, accounts, and records of RAB will be transferred to the SRB.
Existing RAB departmental proceedings rules will remain in effect with necessary adaptations until new regulations are formulated.
caption:
RAB is set to be abolished. A new specialized unit, the Special Response Battalion (SRB), will take its place.

The cabinet has granted final approval to the draft of the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026', following vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.

Under this new law, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) will be abolished and replaced by the Special Response Battalion (SRB), which will operate as a specialized unit under the police force.

The act includes provisions for a multi-party grievance redressal committee to resolve complaints from citizens and internal conflicts among unit members.

All manpower, orders, powers, authority, benefits, funds, properties, accounts, and records of RAB will be transferred to the SRB.

Existing RAB departmental proceedings rules will remain in effect with necessary adaptations until new regulations are formulated.
